title: Streaming-first tool orchestrator with reentrant guards and result provenance
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a streaming-first orchestrator for multi-tool chains that preserves low-latency streams while preventing unbounded recursion and accidental reentrant invocations. The orchestrator will: 1) allow the Core API streaming layer to interleave partial token streams with tool invocation events and progressive tool outputs; 2) inject tool results back into the execution context as structured objects (provenance-tagged) instead of opaque text blobs; 3) enforce reentrancy and loop-safety via a lightweight invocation scoreboard and per-session recursion budget; 4) provide compatibility adapters so older SDK clients (non-streaming or non-structured-output) receive sensible fallbacks. This ticket covers design, a reference implementation (runtime + compatibility shim), tests, and a small migration guide for SDK teams.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Streaming requests that trigger tool chains must be able to emit partial tokens while waiting for tool results and then resume streaming merged outputs without duplicating or stalling the consumer. 2) Every injected tool result must carry a provenance envelope (tool_id, invocation_id, timestamp, checksum) and be accessible to downstream tools/LLM turns. 3) The orchestrator prevents infinite recursion by maintaining a per-session invocation graph and enforcing a configurable max-depth and cost budget; when the budget is exceeded, the orchestrator returns a deterministic fallback response and emits telemetry. 4) Compatibility layer responds to older SDKs by flattening structured outputs into human-readable text with markers and a machine-readable attachment when supported. 5) End-to-end tests cover streaming+tool chains, recursion cutoff, and SDK compatibility for at least Node and Python SDKs. 6) Performance regression against current master is <=10% tail latency for 95th percentile token latency on benchmark harness.
updates: 2026-02-28: Kickoff - scoped initial design and wrote proto spec for 'ProvenanceEnvelope' that wraps tool outputs. Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CORE/Streaming+Orchestrator+Proto

2026-03-03: Spike implemented a local prototype that interleaves stream frames and tool-event frames; observed 2.1x increase in implementation complexity but sub-5ms median added overhead for single-tool calls in a no-op path.

2026-03-05: Design review with API and SDK leads - decided to use a scoreboard approach (weakly-consistent in-memory per-session) instead of global lock to avoid cross-session contention. Action: add garbage collection for long-running sessions.

2026-03-07: UX/SDK decision - compatibility layer will emit 'X-Redwood-Structured: 1' header for streaming clients that understand structured frames; older clients get '[[TOOL-RESULT tool_id=...]]' inline markers. Added Node SDK shim task to scope.
2026-03-09: Security review request filed for tool provenance metadata (possible leakage of sensitive tool identifiers). Ticket: https://security.redwood.ai/reqs/SEC-2026-18

2026-03-10: Integration spike with KV cache - ensured cached responses include provenance and do not count against recursion budget when serving from cache. Noted: need to mark 'served_from_cache' in envelope.

2026-03-12: First internal PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/core/pull/4182 - implements scoreboard, envelope schema, and streaming frame merging. Bench run attached to PR shows 6% p95 token latency regression on synthetic prompt set.
Planned next: add comprehensive unit tests, add Node/Python SDK shims, and run canary on staging with runtime-1.22 profile.
